title: Supervised sweep: student size x teacher (Connect 4 C4Net)
notes: All students are nn.model.C4Net (residual tower, blocks x channels, 7 policy logits, WDL head) trained supervised on the same 300,000 positions of nn_data/solver_300k.npz with the same fixed 95/5 train/val split (split seed 0 = the split of runs/sup_6x64); only teacher and size differ.

Training recipe = nn/train_supervised.py: batch 1024, AdamW lr 2e-3 wd 1e-4, OneCycle, mirror augmentation, bf16 autocast on the RTX 3050, loss = CE(teacher policy) + 1.0 x CE(teacher WDL). best.npz = lowest validation loss against the TEACHER's labels (solver labels are never used to select a non-solver student).

Heuristic teachers (heur_*): for each legal column play it and score the resulting position with the heuristic from the mover's view; a move completing four scores WIN-1 (taken); no other rule (no forced block). This equals engine.minimax.search(depth=1). Policy target = uniform over the columns tied for the best score (hard target, same shape as the Pons target). Value target = tanh(s/sigma) of the best score (sigma = std of that teacher's non-mate best scores; +-1 for proven wins/losses) mapped to (W,D,L) = (max(v,0), 1-|v|, max(-v,0)): a monotone squashing, not a calibrated probability.

Minimax teachers (mm_d4_*): each legal column scored by depth-4 negamax (engine.minimax.search to depth 3 after the move); same target rules as the heuristic teachers. mm_d4_hand = slider level 5 (depth 4, epsilon 0).

Network teachers (ppo_net, ppo_from_sup, sup6x64, sup8x128): soft policy = the network's softmax over legal columns and its WDL output, policy head only, no search/MCTS. Group C (distillation) uses these soft targets on the fixed 300k positions instead of rl/distill.py (which generates its own positions).

Teacher bench numbers: the teacher's own move on the 3,000 held-out solver-scored positions (data/accuracy_positions.csv); agree_pons = share of the 300k positions where the teacher's move is Pons-optimal. Student bench = policy head only, no search.

'6^2 x 64^2' = 36 blocks x 4096 channels would be about 36 * 2 * 9 * 4096^2 = 10.9 billion parameters: not trainable on this hardware (RTX 3050 8 GB). 8x128 (2.4 M parameters) is the top rung of the 1:16 ladder; 10x128 is an optional extra.
Single seed per run unless a _s1 twin exists; benchmark n = 3,000 positions (standard error of an optimal-rate near 0.85 is about 0.0065); gauntlet games are deterministic given the opening.
Gauntlet: 40 openings (nn.bench.random_openings seed 4150, 2-4 plies) x 2 colours vs mm_d1, mm_d2, mm_d4, mm_d6, mm_d4_evo60, distill_az_2x32, sup_6x64.

findings.title: Benchmark accuracy vs network size (solver labels)
findings.claim: On solver labels the optimal-move rate rises by 0.050 per tenfold increase in parameters (R^2 0.72, n=13), from 0.787 at 16994 params to 0.915 at 2971490 params.
findings.caveat: One training schedule for all sizes; bootstrap slope CI [0.02076, 0.07498].

findings.title: Teacher quality predicts student quality (1x16)
findings.claim: Across 3 teachers at 1x16, student optimal-rate vs teacher optimal-rate has Pearson r = -0.12, slope -0.01.
findings.caveat: Teachers differ in kind (hard vs soft targets, value-target definition).

findings.title: Do 2x32 students exceed their search-free / search teachers?
findings.claim: 2 of 7 heuristic/minimax teachers were exceeded in benchmark optimal-rate by their 2x32 student; largest gap +0.004 (heur_hand: teacher 0.729, student 0.733).

findings.title: Teacher quality predicts student quality (2x32)
findings.claim: Across 12 teachers at 2x32, student optimal-rate vs teacher optimal-rate has Pearson r = 0.97, slope 0.70.
findings.caveat: Teachers differ in kind (hard vs soft targets, value-target definition).

findings.title: Teacher quality predicts student quality (3x48)
findings.claim: Across 3 teachers at 3x48, student optimal-rate vs teacher optimal-rate has Pearson r = -0.67, slope -0.08.
findings.caveat: Teachers differ in kind (hard vs soft targets, value-target definition).

findings.title: Teacher quality predicts student quality (4x64)
findings.claim: Across 3 teachers at 4x64, student optimal-rate vs teacher optimal-rate has Pearson r = -0.25, slope -0.03.
findings.caveat: Teachers differ in kind (hard vs soft targets, value-target definition).

findings.title: Do 6x64 students exceed their search-free / search teachers?
findings.claim: 4 of 7 heuristic/minimax teachers were exceeded in benchmark optimal-rate by their 6x64 student; largest gap +0.008 (heur_hand: teacher 0.729, student 0.737).

findings.title: Teacher quality predicts student quality (6x64)
findings.claim: Across 10 teachers at 6x64, student optimal-rate vs teacher optimal-rate has Pearson r = 0.98, slope 0.76.
findings.caveat: Teachers differ in kind (hard vs soft targets, value-target definition).

findings.title: Length of evolved training vs teacher and student quality
findings.claim: No-search evolved-heuristic teachers at generations 0,10,20,40,60 score 0.729, 0.757, 0.746, 0.735, 0.736 optimal; their 2x32 students score 0.733, 0.756, 0.744, 0.738, 0.728.
findings.caveat: Weights were evolved with depth-2 search (runs/evo_d2) and are used here without search.

findings.title: Search vs no-search teacher (hand heuristic)
findings.claim: Teacher optimal-rate 0.729 without search vs 0.873 with depth-4 search; 2x32 students 0.733 vs 0.846.

findings.title: Search vs no-search teacher (evolved gen 60 heuristic)
findings.claim: Teacher optimal-rate 0.736 without search vs 0.878 with depth-4 search; 2x32 students 0.728 vs 0.848.

findings.title: Distilled vs direct at 1x16
findings.claim: At 1x16 (16994 params) the benchmark optimal-rate is: direct 0.787, from 6x64 0.784, from 8x128 0.794.
findings.caveat: Single seed; distillation targets are policy-only soft labels.

findings.title: Distilled vs direct at 2x32
findings.claim: At 2x32 (50146 params) the benchmark optimal-rate is: direct 0.873, from 6x64 0.883, from 8x128 0.869.
findings.caveat: Single seed; distillation targets are policy-only soft labels.

findings.title: Distilled vs direct at 3x48
findings.claim: At 3x48 (138722 params) the benchmark optimal-rate is: direct 0.889, from 6x64 0.900, from 8x128 0.890.
findings.caveat: Single seed; distillation targets are policy-only soft labels.

findings.title: Distilled vs direct at 4x64
findings.claim: At 4x64 (310370 params) the benchmark optimal-rate is: direct 0.904, from 6x64 0.912, from 8x128 0.899.
findings.caveat: Single seed; distillation targets are policy-only soft labels.

findings.title: Seed-to-seed noise
findings.claim: Across 14 size(s) trained with two seeds the optimal-rate differs by at most 0.0100.
